anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: Nothing moved for f4: both outputs select the no-progress row on the unchanged failed `node --test src/guard.test.ts` prerequisite with P1 still open, dispatch no implementer, explicitly decline readiness despite green CI (After even states that run 910 does not cover the mechanism), and render the obstacle as a blocker with a 'fixable' verdict. After's option-1 text ('pick this as the new decision that allows one more attempt') is a reasonable way to frame the required new human decision, though it is wordier than Before's 'the unchanged payload already failed, so name a different approach or it runs again'; if you want to tighten it, keep the explicit statement that the fix grant alone does not trigger a retry and that a different approach must be named, since that sentence is what makes the no-silent-retry behavior visible to the reader. The added compose hints ('revoke fix', 'revoke merge base') and the shared menu layout do not affect this fact.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: Neither output moved f4: both treat the unchanged failed scoped-test prerequisite plus the still-open P1 as a binding no-progress checkpoint, dispatch no helper, run no scoped test, spend no round, and keep the verdict at fixable with one blocker instead of reading green CI run 910 as readiness. After actually states the obstacle more explicitly than Before (the step-4 heading 'Stop automatic repair at the recorded obstacle', the note that the checkpoint takes precedence over both retained grants, and the blocker line 'automatic repair is paused pending a new decision or a change to that prerequisite'), so the menu-layout wording in the Change was delivered without weakening this fact. Keep the explicit 'no new human decision, no change to the prerequisite -> no retry' sentence and the 'CI covers rejection tests only, does not close the mechanism contribution' sentence in any further rewording; those two lines are what carry f4 in both versions.
